title: Candidate trajectory sprint and 12-day activation matrix
content:
Overview:
This one-page working doc pairs a tightened interview progression with a pragmatic 12-day activation plan for new hires joining engineering teams focused on inference and platform services. Its designed to speed hiring decisions while creating a reliable early-impact path for IC2-IC5 hires. Use this as a baseline; teams should adapt the examples to role-specific signals (e.g., quantization knowledge for model runtime roles).

Goals:
- Reduce candidate loop time and variance across panels.
- Surface operational readiness within the first 12 days.
- Create repeatable evidence items for hiring committee decisions.

Process outline (goal: 3 substantive technical touchpoints + cultural/product checks):
1) Recruiter intro (20-30m): alignment on role expectations, logistics, and high-level LLM/infra familiarity. Output: quick pass/no-pass and notes.
2) Short take-home or code kata (max 4h): focused on real-ish tradeoffs (e.g., memory vs latency). Output: scored artifact + author notes.
3) Live technical session (60-90m): systems problem + 15m design probe. Output: rubric scores and 3 concrete evidence bullets.
4) Product/CS cross-functional convo (30-45m): how would candidate make tradeoffs for customers and cost. Output: product-sense notes.
5) Hiring committee / final debrief (30m): composite score and decision.

Key scoring dimensions (uniform 1-5 scale; 1=insufficient, 5=exemplary):
- Technical correctness and clarity
- Systems thinking and operational tradeoffs
- Observability and incident readiness
- Product & customer prioritization
- Collaboration & communication
Keep scoring simple: each interviewer adds 1-3 short evidence lines in the panel sheet. Require a rationale for any 1 or 5.

Practical red flags (fast-fail or require follow-up):
- Evidence of fabricated work or plagiarism on take-homes (fast-fail).
- Candidate cannot explain a basic latency vs cost tradeoff for production (serious signal for infra roles).
- Repeated inability to articulate steps when debugging a live system (fast-fail for mid/senior).

Pre-boarding checklist (owner: People Ops + manager):
- Send offer packet with 2-week orientation schedule and first-90-day expectations.
- Create accounts: SSO, git, cloud project with limited creds, Jira, Confluence, Slack.
- Assign buddy and calendar initial syncs (manager).
- Share short reading list: product one-pager, recent incident postmortem, minimal runtime overview.

12-day activation matrix (practical actions and expected evidence):
Days 0-1 (access, intro, and signals)
- Tasks: confirm SSO, ssh/git access, run a minimal repo example, meet manager and buddy (15-30m).
- Evidence: access checklist in Confluence, 1-paragraph intro posted to team channel.

Days 2-3 (context & observability)
- Tasks: self-guided reads on hosted/dedicated/private modes; walkthrough of Redwood Console dashboards; review an incident timeline.
- Evidence: 3-bullet summary on routing and fallback; one suggested tweak to an existing dashboard or runbook.

Days 4-5 (code onboarding & first PR)
- Tasks: setup dev environment, pick a low-risk starter work item (docs, small telemetry), pair to open PR.
- Evidence: PR opened with description tying the change to product metrics; CI green or plan to address failures.

Days 6-7 (ops simulation & metrics)
- Tasks: run a 30-45m tabletop incident with buddy; instrument a simple metric or synthetic test.
- Evidence: post-incident notes and one PR/Confluence update to improve a threshold or alert.

Days 8-9 (owner-lite feature and experiment design)
- Tasks: propose a small experiment (e.g., KV cache hit-rate metric by route) and implement a minimal tracking signal.
- Evidence: draft experiment doc plus code changes or dashboard draft.

Days 10-11 (customer context and cross-team feedback)
- Tasks: sit in a CS/customer call focused on Dedicated/Private deployment; collect operational pain points.
- Evidence: 2 suggestions for short-term improvements posted and tagged, ask for feedback from CS within 48h.

Day 12 (first-impact review)
- Tasks: 30-45m sync with manager to review PRs, experiments, incident notes, and readiness.
- Evidence: 30/60/90 plan in Confluence and a decision: "on-track" or list of targeted gaps.

Owners (suggested):
- Manager: defines first project and acceptance criteria.
- Buddy: daily check-ins and tabletop partner.
- People Ops: logistics, benefits, and first-week pulse check.
- Platform/infra mentor: dev env, starter issue, and security gating.

Early-hire signals for fast-tracking into active projects:
- PR quality and timely review responses (<=72h).
- Can explain a production tradeoff in 3 succinct bullets.
- Proposed runbook tweak or dashboard change merged or approved.

Templates and short artifacts to include with the doc:
- 1-page "Day-12 acceptance" checklist (checkboxes + one-paragraph context).
- Panel scoring sheet template with short-evidence slots.
- 4-hour infra take-home prompt focusing on latency-memory tradeoffs.
- 30-45m incident tabletop script tailored to inference serving.

Next steps and experiments to run:
- Pilot an auto-harness for take-homes (unit tests + similarity check) to reduce reviewer time.
- Trial a 1-week paid contractor sprint for senior IC hires to reduce interview loop length.
- Feed hiring outcome signals into People Ops analytics to refine funnel metrics.

Revision history:
- 2025-04-15 Draft by Harper Chen
- 2025-04-18 Feedback from hiring partners (Aisha, Liam)
- 2025-04-22 Updated activation pacing and added experiment items

Notes-to-self: keep this concise, iterate after 3 hires, track time-in-loop metrics.
